parent.behavior_scope: accepted local LRU demand with one spare and explicit 10-minute REMOVE, 20-minute REPLACE

prerequisite.behavior_scope: accepted local removed-LRU direct repair, restock and reissue before a later demand

source.source_boundary: System replacement demands a spare immediately when repair starts. REMOVE can release the faulty LRU for local ItemRepair. REPLACE cannot begin without a spare. With zero stock, the demand becomes a local backorder; an item returned from repair serves that backorder before entering stock.

delta.mechanism: Change only local repairable-LRU nominal stock STSIZ from 1 to 0, retaining the accepted one-failure seed, explicit system replacement steps and one-hour local ItemRepair.

predeclared_native_acceptance: The frozen seed/configuration must produce at least one observed installed-LRU failure. Exact stochastic time is taken from raw native events.

The first system replacement demand must find zero on-hand stock and create a backorder. REMOVE must complete before the removed LRU enters one-hour local ItemRepair; the system must wait to begin REPLACE until that repaired item returns and serves the backorder.

Trace physical item identity through removal, ItemRepair, backorder clearance, receipt and installation. Reconcile waiting time and system readiness with the one-spare E01 control, and show the repaired item arrives before the next mission deadline.

Import/export must preserve all 20 row-containing source tables, including three all-null placeholders; conversion errors must be zero, four native CLI steps must succeed, and 72 half-hour system/stock intervals must reconcile with events.
Use session-0 SSH under the host-wide native queue, preserve GUI PID 13340, seal raw hashes and obtain independent read-only replay.
limits: This is a single local stockout/backorder served by repair of the removed item. It does not accept remote or lateral supply, multiple simultaneous demands, FIFO ordering, reorder, resource contention or PM.
Exact failure time is run-specific; the native event log, not the input seed alone, supplies timing evidence.
